source.title: Abra: Scaling Diffusion Image Training
source.authors: Kyle R. Chickering; Wei-An Lin; Swayam Bhanded; D. Saunders; Akshat Tripathi; Jia-Ming Song; S. Buch; Xin-Chen Yan

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It extends compute-optimal scaling analysis to text-to-image diffusion models, measuring held-out evaluation loss and compute-optimal allocations in an image-generation setting.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own scaling results for diffusion-model evaluation loss, allocation, generative metrics, and linear-probe accuracy. Results it cites from other studies, including the LLM comparisons, are not recorded as this study's results. The appendix's comparisons among fitting procedures are included where they report changes in the study's fitted optimum.
record.test_reason: The study trains its own ladder of text-to-image flow-matching transformers (60M–2B, 1e19–1e22 FLOPs). It fits power laws to held-out EMA evaluation loss, generative metrics and linear-probe accuracy, and estimates compute-optimal allocation with Kaplan- and Hoffmann-style estimators. That is a new modality with direct results on whether the scaling-law form transfers (V5) and on how fitting and setup choices move the optimum (V7).
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Add that the authors conclude diffusion training is robust to overtraining (err toward more data), that representation quality scales with a much lower and rising optimal TPP than generation, and that compute-optimal diffusion training shows scaling collapse. They state that about 200 TPP is invariant across fit methods.
record.recipe_differences: This is a controlled text-to-image flow-matching diffusion study rather than language-model pretraining. It uses EMA-weight held-out evaluation loss, image tokens, and iso-FLOP allocation fits; it also examines resolution, generative metrics, and linear probes.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported compute-optimal TPP changes with image resolution (165 at 256 × 256 to 247 at 768 × 768). Using raw training loss rather than EMA-weight evaluation loss changes the excluded-60M estimate from 199 to 227 TPP. Including the identified 60M outlier changes the headline estimate from 199 to 186 TPP. Other tested estimator and interpolation variations are reported to be comparatively stable.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed compute, 2× overtraining costs under 0.5% eval loss, while undertraining is catastrophic.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Diffusion models tolerate overtraining far better than LLMs at fixed compute.

fits_no_version.finding: Rescaled training curves of 60M, 120M and 250M models collapse to within the seed-noise floor after the first 15% of training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Compute-optimal diffusion training shows scaling collapse of loss-curve shape.

fits_no_version.finding: Optimal CFG scale decreases with both model size and training compute (Fig. 19).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimal guidance strength falls predictably with scale in diffusion models.

record.problems: The study tests one controlled model family and keeps the optimizer, text encoder, vision encoder, and other choices fixed; the authors identify these as limitations. A BRA-60M is a stated outlier, and the resolution fits assume balanced allocation because the largest models there are only 500M. Some reported fit uncertainty is described as evaluation noise rather than a confidence interval.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant own-result rows were omitted. Cited LLM results and the cited prior diffusion study's results were not recorded as this paper's findings.

untested.parts: No language-model pretraining loss. The analogous diffusion loss result is recorded under V5.
No held-out extrapolation test. The 5e22 FLOP / 6B 'double-point' is an unverified extrapolation.
LM compute-optimal allocation is not tested. The diffusion allocation exponents (near balanced) are recorded under V5.
Depth and width co-vary along the ladder. There is no fixed-N shape ablation.
Not tested: video, fine-tuning, transfer, and repeated data as a manipulated variable (epochs reach 7.7 but are not varied).
Not tested: LM downstream tasks, and downstream performance as a function of pretraining loss. Only the ImageNet linear probe versus compute is reported.
Not tested: optimizer, text encoder, vision encoder, batch-size scaling and data distribution (authors list these as limitations).

missing.what: Robustness of TPP* to other estimators and variations: Kaplan 192, supporting hyperplane 192, Hoffmann A1 192, Huber 199, linear interpolation 202, drop-2B 195 (excl. 60M).
Leave-one-model-out TPP* stays within 188–207 with 60M excluded.
The Hoffmann Approach 3 parametric loss surface is non-identifiable on this ladder.
Including or excluding embedding parameters shifts optimal TPP by less than 3%.
Each of ten timestep buckets obeys its own power law in compute, with differing exponents.
Metric scaling exponents are stable across fixed CFG values, with a mild decline at high CFG for CMMD and CLIPScore.
The own allocation exponent (a=0.495 constrained) is compared with Liang et al.'s 0.568 for diffusion transformers.

record.verdict_notes: Diffusion-model allocation rows were moved from V3 to V5, because V3 names the LM recipes and the rows must match the kind of system. V6 and V7 are not LM-specific and were kept. The reader's V3 'supports' label is replaced by the V5 label. Rows R6–R9 impose a=b=0.5, so they speak only to the TPP ratio, not the exponents. Cited LLM penalty curves (Gemstones, Chinchilla, Gadre, Porian) are correctly not rows.

versions.untested_parts: The study trains image diffusion models, not language models, and does not test held-out language-model pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
It fits scaling relationships across its model ladder but does not report a test in which fits from small runs predict the loss of much larger runs.
Tests compute-optimal parameter and image-token allocation for this diffusion-model family; it does not test the language-model-specific allocation recipes on language models.
It does not hold parameter count fixed while systematically varying depth, width, or other architecture details to measure their effect on loss.
Tests image diffusion pretraining. It does not test video, fine-tuning, transfer, or whether the same law holds across other training regimes.
Tests ImageNet linear-probe accuracy, not a broad range of downstream tasks or the relationship between downstream performance and pretraining loss.

Tests sensitivity to fitting target and image resolution and notes a small-model outlier. It does not ablate all listed factors, such as optimizers, text encoders, vision encoders, or data distributions.

relationships.reason: EMA eval loss follows L=A C^-α+β. Optimal N and D grow as stable powers near 0.5. Generative metrics and probe accuracy follow compute power laws (R1, R3, R4, R6–R13, R15, R16).
relationships.display_finding: Evaluation loss follows L = A·C^-α + β, optimal parameter and data sizes scale with exponents near 0.5, and generation metrics and probe accuracy follow compute power laws.
